treatment: Sequential methotrexate/fluorouracil + leucovorin vs surgery alone
population: 760 women with ER-negative, node-negative breast cancer
benefitText: Eight-year DFS was 74% vs 59%, an absolute improvement of 15 percentage points.
harmText: No single dominant fixed-time toxicity endpoint supports a defensible NNH.
clinicalInterpretation: B-13 established substantial benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy in ER-negative node-negative disease.
clinicalQuestion: Does adjuvant methotrexate/fluorouracil improve outcomes over surgery alone?
refs: Fisher B, et al. J Clin Oncol. 1996;14:1982–1992.

population: About 2,844 women with ER-positive, node-negative breast cancer
benefitText: Five-year DFS was 82% vs 72%, an absolute improvement of 10 percentage points.
harmText: No single dominant fixed-time harm endpoint supports an NNH.
clinicalInterpretation: B-14 was foundational randomized evidence for adjuvant tamoxifen in ER-positive node-negative breast cancer.
clinicalQuestion: Does five years of tamoxifen improve outcomes compared with placebo?

population: 1,095 women with ER-negative, node-negative breast cancer
benefitText: Five-year DFS was 82% vs 73%, an absolute improvement of 9 percentage points.
harmText: CMF had more grade ≥3 toxicity, but a single fixed-time dominant endpoint was not suitable for NNH.
clinicalInterpretation: Adding cyclophosphamide produced a clear DFS gain, especially in younger women.
clinicalQuestion: Does adding cyclophosphamide to MF improve outcomes?
refs: Fisher B, et al. J Clin Oncol. 1996;14:1982–1992.

population: 6,846 women with ER-positive early breast cancer for efficacy analyses
benefitText: Recurrence during years 5–14 was 21.4% vs 25.1%; breast-cancer mortality was 12.2% vs 15.0%.
harmText: Endometrial cancer increased by 1.5 percentage points during years 5–14.
clinicalInterpretation: Continuing tamoxifen to 10 years produced modest absolute reductions in recurrence and breast-cancer mortality, with a measurable endometrial-cancer trade-off.
clinicalQuestion: Does continuing tamoxifen to 10 years improve outcomes after 5 years of therapy?

treatment: Tamoxifen + ovarian suppression vs tamoxifen alone
benefitText: Eight-year DFS was 83.2% vs 78.9%. Exemestane + ovarian suppression reached 85.9%.
harmText: Grade ≥3 adverse events increased by 6.4 percentage points with tamoxifen + ovarian suppression.
clinicalInterpretation: Ovarian suppression adds an absolute disease-control benefit, with greater benefit from exemestane plus ovarian suppression in higher-risk patients.
clinicalQuestion: Does ovarian suppression added to endocrine therapy improve outcomes in premenopausal breast cancer?
refs: Francis PA, et al. N Engl J Med. 2018;378:436–446.

benefitText: Five-year relapse-free survival was 96.1% vs 96.2%; relapse rates were very low in both groups.
harmText: Para-aortic-only treatment reduced acute toxicity and gonadal toxicity.
clinicalInterpretation: Field reduction maintained very high overall disease control while reducing treatment morbidity.
clinicalQuestion: Can para-aortic-only RT replace dog-leg RT in stage I seminoma?
refs: Fossa SD, et al. J Clin Oncol. 1999;17:1146.

population: 337 randomized patients with intermediate-prognosis germ-cell cancer
benefitText: Three-year PFS was 79.4% vs 71.1% in the ITT analysis. The primary analysis did not reach statistical significance.
harmText: No single dominant fixed-time toxicity endpoint supports a defensible NNH.
clinicalInterpretation: The trial was under-accrued; the eligible-patient analysis showed a larger PFS signal, but the primary ITT analysis remains the key result.
clinicalQuestion: Does adding paclitaxel to BEP improve PFS in intermediate-prognosis germ-cell cancer?
refs: de Wit R, et al. J Clin Oncol. 2012;30:792–799.

treatment: Deferred vs immediate cytoreductive nephrectomy with sunitinib
benefitText: 28-week PFR was 43% vs 42%. The study was underpowered after poor accrual.
harmText: No fixed-time randomized harm endpoint supports NNH.
clinicalInterpretation: Initial systemic therapy can select patients for surgery and avoid nephrectomy in those with early progression.
clinicalQuestion: Should sunitinib precede cytoreductive nephrectomy in synchronous metastatic RCC?
refs: Bex A, et al. JAMA Oncol. 2019.

population: 915 previously untreated patients with metastatic RCC; 362 PD-L1 positive
benefitText: Twelve-month PFS was 49% vs 38% in PD-L1-positive disease.
nnH: Not quantifiable as a harm because the combination had fewer events
harmText: Grade 3–4 treatment-related adverse events were 40% vs 54% in the primary analysis.
clinicalInterpretation: The trial met its PD-L1-positive PFS endpoint but did not demonstrate an OS benefit in final analyses.
clinicalQuestion: Does atezolizumab plus bevacizumab improve outcomes versus sunitinib in first-line metastatic RCC?

population: 153 patients with high-risk nonmetastatic urothelial MIBC after radical cystectomy and chemotherapy
benefitText: Two-year locoregional control was 91.2% vs 76.4%, an absolute improvement of 14.8 points.
harmText: Late grade ≥3 toxicity was 8.5% with RT vs 10.5% with observation.
clinicalInterpretation: BART provides randomized phase III evidence for substantial reduction in pelvic relapse with postoperative RT without increased severe late toxicity.
clinicalQuestion: Does adjuvant pelvic RT reduce locoregional relapse after cystectomy and chemotherapy in high-risk MIBC?
